q1_issues.issue: No (Past ...) status atom although the clause is past tense ("There was nothing to be seen"), so the seeing event is left unmarked/habitual.
(Can sk_see_1) asserts a capability the sentence never states — the instruction set licenses Can only for "can / able to", not for a bare infinitival "to be seen".
The negative existential ("there was nothing ...") has no carrier: the parse asserts a positive seeing event and records the exclusivity only through the opaque Only tag.

q2_gaps: exceptive "but" after a negative quantifier ("nothing / no one ... but X") — the negative-existential-plus-exception construction; the focus-particle section covers only "only / just / solely"
infinitival passive relative "nothing to be seen" — a modal-flavoured to-infinitive with no overt modal and no expressed perceiver
notes: Routing "nothing but fog" through Only is a defensible improvisation and the bare mass constant fog (no Member atom) is right, but the past tense is simply lost and Can has no licensing cue in the text.
